title: Back Again (Yes, the Grok 20k Guy).
author: Moedawi85
selftext:
Aight, I’m back with changed strategy and profitable 1st day. After going back and forth with Grok, Claude, and DeepSeek like some kind of AI custody battle, I decided to go for a bit rather than the whole slice.

I needed this thing to be (FAST AS FUCK BOIIII) lol. Since I already have DeepSeek’s API hooked up in my trading app (and previously had it just monitoring one of the bots), I figured I’d let it take a bite instead of waiting around for the whole pie. I handed Deep the penny stock trades, told it things were about to get spicy, and gave it the green light for up to a 5% spread.

The rules are simple:

1. Deep has to stay on its toes and be Fast As F\*\*\* (no daydreaming)

2. Only buy if something pops 5% or more in 30 seconds

3. Take the 5% and get out

4. Only trade from 9:30 to 11

Claude’s backtests came back with negative numbers, which was… not ideal. But then I started watching the actual candles take off 10 to 20% in seconds and figured, maybe the backtest is just being dramatic. So I adjusted the rules and decided to let Deep run it live anyway.

Gonna keep this going for a couple of weeks and see what actually happens in the real market. Wish me luck (or roast me later if it faceplants).

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: so the 9:31 halt rule got retired for this? a 5% spread allowance on penny names is a lot to hand over on every entry, the stock has to climb that far just to get you back to even when you sell at the bid. one green day says very little here, the first red open is the one that'll tell you.

replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body: I allowed it up to 5% and the reason for that i wanna see how often it catches that 5% and win rate so will let it run and log the spread vs profit, and after lets say a month and then the fine turning starts

replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body:
Im not gonna lie I feel like DeepSeek is slightly better and straight forward and alot faster than Claude, it's API is built in the app so it recommends trades from my scanner and anything I buy it logs to a ledger but when I sell it doesn't sell on the ledge so few trades it recommends to buy and 2 days later they made that much, obviously not everything it recommends makes money but it's long frame readings are solid.

https://reddit.com/link/1y1ecg0/video/4ln7f8b67u2i1/player

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the ledger missing sells is what I'd fix before anything else, because without exits logged you can't tell what that 5% spread allowance is costing you. simplest version: one row per fill, buy or sell, with the quote it saw at that moment, and P&L computed from fills, not from what the model recommended.

replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body: That all logged at every trade but I the reason why I logs the trads in the ledger was my request previously just to see when my losses go after selling or keep hammering myself that I should've kept the tickers lol. Actually I will create a sheet and share it with the community here cuz like I said I dont mind sharing a working strategy

replies.body: a shared sheet would be useful, almost nobody posts their sells. up 20k then gone in two weeks on halts is a lesson plenty of people pay for, and the log is how you avoid paying twice. to try the 5% spread idea without money first, I built Quantradin, the one I mentioned in October, for running a rule like that on paper. quantradin.com

comments.author: cybersarcasm
comments.body: How long did you test for? What were the scoring limits on the trades? Did you pull any historical data? Which strategy are you utilizing? How are you maintaining checks and balances?

replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body: If u wanna consider it new strategy it's 1 day, if u wanna look at it as updates to the strategy making it looser and faster then about 2 weeks and maybe won 2 or 3 days positive out of the 10 plus days down 5k. Give me till friday I'll post what u mentioned

comments.author: Interesting_Gold_792
comments.body: Respect for running it live and posting it. One thing I'd check before trusting week one: with a 5% spread allowed, a 5% take-profit can get mostly eaten by fills on the way in and out. Log your actual fill vs the signal price on every trade, and compare against random entries in the same window. When the backtest says negative, live usually agrees once enough trades pile up. Genuinely curious how it goes.

replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body: This is paper trading now, im saving all the logs and will share the 1st log maybe friday, comparing this strategy to how it runs now is looser picks, and strict fast exit, i know the spread is allowed up to 5% and thats why the logs at the end of the week would let me know if the5% is ok or if i can up my take profit percentage.

replies.author: Interesting_Gold_792
replies.body: Makes sense, logging it on paper first is the right call. One tip for Friday: log the spread at entry next to the profit on each trade, then bucket the trades by spread size. If the wide-spread trades are the losers, you've found your cutoff without guessing. Looking forward to the log.
